faq.a: Siti is associated with the Arabic form سِيتِي, whose core sense is siti; lady (indonesian form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Siti?
faq.a: Siti is associated with Arabic. Siti is the Indonesian/Malay form of Arabic سِتّ (sitt), meaning 'lady'. It is widely used as a female given name, often before a name such as Siti Aisyah.
Yes — the underlying form سِيتِي is Arabic.
Siti can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Siti should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Sitt is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Siti mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Siti is rendered سيتي and carries the sense سيتي، خاتون.

faq.q: What does Siti mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Siti is rendered سیتی and carries the sense سیتی، بانو.
A romanized syllable approximation is si-ti. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Siti?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Siti, siti. Script forms are سيتي, سِيتِي, سیتی, सीती.

faq.q: Is Siti a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
